claim: The standing policy for on-screen text, which is otherwise the most reliable generation artefact in any populated exterior. Blurred and none are the working choices that survive a render; ja and invented are the ones that tell the audience what world they are in.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: japanese text, kanji signage, japanese billboard
english text, latin letters, english signage
blank signs, unmarked surfaces, no lettering
fictional script, invented alphabet, alien lettering
blurry text, illegible signage, out of focus lettering

review.issue: The none clause ends on "no lettering", a negation that will tend to produce lettering. "blank signs" and "unmarked surfaces" already carry the option on their own.
review.fix: "blank signs, unmarked surfaces, plain white panels" — and put "text, watermark, signature" in the negative prompt for this panel.
